subject.title: fix(hooks): bound hook workspace manifest and HOOK.md reads

question: Should workspace hook package.json and HOOK.md metadata larger than 1 MiB be rejected with a warning, accepting that existing oversized hooks may stop loading?
rationale: The implementation is sound, but the threshold intentionally narrows an existing user-controlled metadata contract and therefore requires maintainer ownership of the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept 1 MiB warn-and-skip
options.body: Land the current behavior, matching the merged install-path boundary while preserving discovery of other hooks and manifest fallback.

options.title: Choose a different cap
options.body: Select a higher limit and update the workspace and install-path policy or tests as needed to keep hook metadata handling consistent.

options.title: Retain unlimited reads
options.body: Decline this hardening and preserve compatibility with arbitrarily large metadata at the cost of the memory-exhaustion exposure.

recommendation.title: Accept 1 MiB warn-and-skip
recommendation.body: Land the current behavior, matching the merged install-path boundary while preserving discovery of other hooks and manifest fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent hook loader, test-boundary, install-safety, and integrity work makes him the strongest available owner for this compatibility and hardening decision.
